title: Here's our first look—and drive—of the 2027 Range Rover Electric
gist: Jaguar Land Rover debuted the 2027 Range Rover Electric at $138,000 on the existing powertrain-agnostic MLA architecture, with a 118.5 kWh AESC NMC pack at 800 V, 542 hp combined, 333 miles of EPA range and 350 kW peak charging. JLR claims 80,000 hand-raisers, half in North America, 70 percent new to the brand and only 20 percent already EV owners.

insights.claim: Jaguar Land Rover says it already has 80,000 hand-raisers for the Range Rover Electric, half from North America, with 70 percent new to the brand and only 20 percent already owning an EV.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A luxury BEV pulling mostly first-time brand buyers who are also first-time EV buyers is the conquest profile OEMs need; the caveat the author flags is that only some fraction converts to sales.
insights.locator: Jaguar Land Rover was one of the first automakers

insights.claim: At a starting price of $138,000 the Range Rover Electric is about half the cost of an electric restomod of a classic Range Rover while adding airbags, advanced driver assistance systems, modern crash protection, and OEM warranty support.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: OEM entry at half the aftermarket price effectively closes the electric-restomod niche for this platform.
insights.locator: Until now, the only way to get a fully electric Range Rover

insights.claim: The design brief was to make the vehicle a Range Rover first and an EV second, so it looks virtually identical to combustion versions apart from a smoother grille, more aero-efficient wheels, a flat underbody and the absence of tailpipes.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Brand continuity over EV signaling is the emerging luxury playbook after several OEMs found dedicated EV styling suppressed conquest demand.
insights.locator: Because the idea was to make the Range Rover Electric

insights.claim: JLR states that 40 percent of Range Rover owners say they go off-road while the brand's own analytics indicate the real figure is closer to 10 percent, yet off-road capability was treated as non-negotiable for the BEV.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A 4x gap between claimed and actual usage shows how much engineering cost in this segment is spent on capability that functions as brand signaling.
insights.locator: Forty percent of Range Rover owners say they go off-road

insights.claim: The Range Rover Electric rides on JLR's MLA architecture, designed over a decade ago to be powertrain agnostic, and the BEV weighs only 165 lbs more than the V8 because deleting the front, center and rear differentials plus driveshafts offsets almost all the battery and drive unit mass.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A decade-old flexible architecture is delivering a near weight-neutral BEV variant without a dedicated EV platform — a capex argument against ground-up EV skateboards for low-volume luxury.

insights.claim: The battery pack's aluminum frame makes the chassis 56 percent stiffer and lowers the center of gravity 3.4 inches versus the V8, while the vehicle is 7 decibels quieter without the V8's noise, vibration and harshness.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Structural and NVH gains are where electrification actually improves a luxury SUV product, independent of any emissions rationale.

insights.claim: JLR rejected a quad-motor layout like Rivian's top-spec R1 as too heavy for the first electric Range Rover, having experimented with a four-motor system back in the 1990s, and dropped a front induction motor over heat management concerns.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Motor-count decisions in premium electric SUVs are being made on mass and thermal grounds, not capability — a check on the assumption that quad-motor becomes the segment standard.
insights.locator: As for why there’s no quad-motor layout

insights.claim: The 118.5 kWh net pack uses AESC nickel-manganese-cobalt cells in a double stack of 10 modules with aerogel spacers, operates at 800 V, and runs two virtual twins that help the active battery management calculate performance.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: AESC secures a flagship 800 V NMC design win in the luxury SUV segment, and the digital-twin BMS approach is becoming table stakes at this price point.
insights.locator: In a nice bit of packaging

insights.claim: The vehicle offers at least 333 miles of EPA range — described as sufficient for 97 percent of owners' daily needs — a native NACS port with Supercharger access, ISO15118 plug-and-charge, 350 kW DC peak charging adding 125 miles in 10 minutes, and a 22-minute 10-80 percent time.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Native NACS on a European luxury flagship confirms the standard's consolidation in North America and removes adapters as a purchase objection.
insights.locator: On a full charge, the Range Rover Electric

insights.claim: The ThermAssist heat management system recaptures waste energy to boost range by 7 percent and cut the energy needed to heat the car by 40 percent.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Thermal management is delivering range gains comparable to meaningful battery capacity additions at far lower cost and weight.
insights.locator: The powertrain also recaptures waste energy

insights.claim: The front and rear drive units are identical 349 hp permanent-magnet synchronous motors for 542 hp and 627 lb-ft combined, are 24 percent more efficient than those in the I-Pace, respond in 50 ms, and use silicon-carbide inverters that react in under a millisecond.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A 24 percent efficiency gain over the prior generation quantifies the pace of e-motor improvement, and silicon carbide is now standard content at this tier.
insights.locator: The front and rear drive units are identical

insights.claim: The Range Rover Electric supports up to 3.6 kW of AC vehicle-to-load output, with vehicle-to-grid support planned for the future.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: V2G being deferred rather than shipped shows the grid-services value proposition is still not commercially compelling enough for OEMs to launch with.
insights.locator: The Range Rover Electric is capable of providing up to 3.6 kW

insights.claim: The vehicle hits 0-60 mph in 4.3 seconds benchmarked against the V8, carries 6,195 lbs of curb weight on air suspension with twin-valve dampers, has 7.3 degrees of rear steering, and offers optional one-pedal driving regenerating up to 0.2 G.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Performance was targeted at parity with the outgoing V8 rather than at EV-typical acceleration bragging, consistent with the brand-first positioning.

insights.claim: Ground clearance drops to 10.3 inches, 1.2 inches less than the V8 because the rear drive unit sits lower than the rear differential, but the vehicle forded water up to 36 inches deep and handled rocks and mud ruts on JLR's Gaydon course.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: The only measurable off-road regression from electrification is 1.2 inches of clearance — a much smaller penalty than the segment feared.
insights.locator: Ground clearance is up to 10.3 inches

insights.claim: The electric version has no center or locking differentials, relying instead on an integrated torque management system that constantly manages front and rear axles by sensing available grip.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Software torque vectoring displacing mechanical lockers removes hardware cost and complexity from off-road-capable vehicles — a structural headwind for driveline component suppliers.
insights.locator: Unlike the V8, there’s no center diff

insights.claim: JLR added extra isolation to the front drive unit and paid particular attention to high-voltage cables that can conduct noise and vibration into the cabin, and fitted an active noise cancellation system using very thin membrane speakers developed with Warwick Audio and mounted in the seat headrests.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Removing engine noise exposes previously masked NVH paths, creating new supplier opportunities in isolation and active noise cancellation for EVs.
insights.locator: An inherent advantage of electric propulsion
